chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Hashem, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Omayr, on the authority of Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of As-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn Al-Hussein; on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was questioned about the meaning of what God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'I will leave behind two heavy things with you: God’s Book and my ‘Itra.' He was asked, 'What does “my ‘Itra” mean?' He replied, 'It is I, Al-Hasan, Al-Hussein and the nine Imams from the descendants of Al-Hussein. The ninth of them is their Al-Mahdi (Divinely Guided One) who is their Riser. They will not separate themselves from God’s Book, and God’s Book will not separate from them until they meet God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) at his Pool.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Itra (Progeny) mentioned in the Hadith of the Two Weighty Things?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* provides a definitive Shia exegesis of the Hadith al-Thaqalayn, explicitly identifying the 'Itra as the Prophet, his grandsons Hasan and Husayn, and the nine Imams descending from Husayn, with the ninth being the Mahdi. It underscores the theological principle of *la tafaruqu* (inseparability), asserting that the Quran and the Imams will never be separated until they meet at the Prophet’s Hawd, thereby establishing the Imams as the living embodiment of the Quran's guidance.
